q: 2026 NBA Finals Game 4, New York Knicks beat San Antonio Spurs 107-106 on June 10, 2026 after trailing by 29 points. Was this the largest comeback in NBA Finals history (and playoff history)? What was the previous record? Give exact sources with URLs. Also list quotes from Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Mitch Johnson, Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby, Mike Brown after the game, about Fox's late layup attempt that was blocked and Anunoby's game-winning tip-in.
text:
Yes, the New York Knicks' incredible 29-point comeback victory over the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4 of the 2026 NBA Finals was indeed the **largest comeback in NBA Finals history**. However, it was **not** the largest comeback in overall NBA Playoff history. 

Here is the breakdown of the records:
* **NBA Finals Record:** The Knicks' 29-point rally broke the previous NBA Finals record of **24 points**, set by the Boston Celtics against the Los Angeles Lakers in Game 4 of the 2008 Finals. 
* **NBA Playoff Record:** The overall playoff record remains **31 points**, which was set by the Los Angeles Clippers against the Golden State Warriors in Game 2 of the first round of the 2019 NBA Playoffs.

### Exact Sources & URLs

* **CBS News / AP:** *"Knicks complete record rally from 29 points down and beat Spurs 107-106 for 3-1 NBA Finals lead"* – [https://www.cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com) / [https://www.washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com)
* **CBS Sports:** *"Guard explains layup blunder in Spurs' Game 4 meltdown vs. Knicks"* – [https://www.cbssports.com](https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/)

### Postgame Quotes (Game 4)
The sequence of De'Aaron Fox attempting a fast-break layup instead of draining the clock, getting blocked cleanly by OG Anunoby, and Anunoby subsequently tipping in Jalen Brunson's missed 3-pointer with 1.2 seconds left generated massive reactions. Here is what the key figures said after the game:

**De'Aaron Fox (Spurs Guard)** 
On his highly criticized decision to attack the rim instead of pulling the ball out to draw a foul and run out the clock:
> *"I just thought I'd be able to outrun him. That's it."*

**OG Anunoby (Knicks Forward)** 
Delivering his signature deadpan, understated reaction despite hitting the biggest shot of his career:
> *"It feels cool. I mean, everyone's pretty excited. I'm excited, too."*

**Jalen Brunson (Knicks Guard/Finals MVP)** 
Praising Anunoby's heroics and impact after the tip-in:
> *"OG is someone who brings it every night, does what's asked of him every single night... Regardless of what the outside world thinks of him, we have a superstar in that locker room."*

**Victor Wembanyama (Spurs Center)** 
Addressing the heartbreaking defeat and his own struggles (including missing two crucial late free throws) in the postgame press conference:
> *"What's going through my mind right now is gonna go one of two ways. A bad one and a good one. The bad one would be giving up, the good one would be getting stronger through this. It's simple as that, it just hurts."*

**Mitch Johnson (Spurs Head Coach)** 
On the devastating second-half collapse and blown 29-point lead:
> *"We got on our heels — we missed some shots. It's disappointing, to say the least."*

**Mike Brown (Knicks Head Coach)** 
On Anunoby's unbelievable effort to clean up Brunson's miss and complete the historic comeback:
> *"I told OG as big, as strong, as athletic as he is, he's got to be a monster on the offensive glass tonight. I don't know if there was a play bigger than any other play in the history of Knicks basketball... That has to be the most iconic shot in the history of New York basketball."*
